article_title: Beyond AI Multiples: The Value in Boring Businesses
news_headline: CoreWeave's market confidence erodes as bond yields spike and stock sinks
post_text:
CoreWeave's stock has fallen 36% in October alone. Its 2031 bonds are yielding nearly 16%, credit default swaps are pricing in better-than-60% odds of default within five years, and HSBC analysts now argue the company's return on invested capital sits below its cost of borrowing. The neocloud built its entire model on cheap debt to fund GPU infrastructure, and with rates higher and AI revenue growth slowing, that math is collapsing in public view.

This isn't just a CoreWeave problem. Oracle's investment-grade CDS spreads have blown out 311% year-over-year. Goldman Sachs tracked $106 billion in AI-related project financing this year. Junk bond buyers are freezing out new AI issuers entirely. The whole AI build-out assumed indefinitely cheap capital and indefinitely fast revenue ramp, neither held.

WBR's piece 'Beyond AI Multiples: The Value in Boring Businesses' made this case before the cracks showed. Capital sprinting toward 30x revenue AI bets was always ignoring a basic question: what happens when the debt comes due and the returns aren't there? CoreWeave is now that question, live. The article is on the WBR website.

#WBR #Finance
